text:
Jordan (PM): Hey folks — quick sync. I'm assembling the launch staffing matrix + handoff doc for the next feature release. Need owners for: SLA tiers, surge policy, billing gates, support concierge pilot, and runbook handback. Can people pick owners and call out any blockers by EOD? :wave:
Ravi (Eng): I can own the surge policy + fallback routing docs. Will draft autoscale boundaries and a short checklist for model fallback. ETA tomorrow noon.
Sam (SRE): I'll take the SLA targets and runbook handback. Want to confirm: are we committing to 99.9% per-route latency at GA or a graduated SLA?
Jordan (PM): Good Q. Proposal: GA = 99.5% latency SLO for hosted tier, with 99.9% as a mission for Dedicated. We should capture exceptions for long-tail prompts. Thoughts?
Lena (Support): For concierge pilot, we need 2 on-call reps for first 2 weeks of GA (shift overlap for first 3 days). I'll staff the rota but need approvals on overtime budget from FinOps. Also: escalation ladder in runbook must include clear contact at Eng + SRE.
Marcus (FinOps): Overtime ok within capped pilot budget. Need expected token-volume estimate + burn rate to finalize. Jordan — can you paste projected QPS and token counts?
Jordan (PM): Sure — projected steady QPS 40, peak 160 (20% headroom). Token mix: avg 80 tokens/req, bursty up to 3k tokens for long-form. I'll add numbers to the doc.
Priya (Docs): I'll own the handoff doc and public docs updates. Plan to split into 1) internal runbook 2) public SLA page 3) ops checklist. Ask: do we want to include the exact latency numbers publicly or keep them internal?
Olivia (Security): We'll need a short section on data residency and KMS controls for Private deployments before GA. If Priya needs a stub, I can write a paragraph. Also need SOC audit timeline included if customers ask.
Ravi (Eng): One blocker: model quantization profile for Dedicated isn't finalized. That affects cost and perf numbers for SLA. I can mark it as a risk and put a mitigation: fallback to verified quantized variant or auto-scale up to burst capacity.
Sam (SRE): For runbook snippets, use this command to escalate to platform oncall:
```
/ops escalate --sev P1 --service inference-runtime --contact platform-oncall
```
Make sure it's copy/paste ready in the doc.
deploy-bot: New doc created: https://redwood.internal/docs/launch-handshake/1769500000 — Jordan (PM) is the creator. :white_check_mark:
Marcus (FinOps): Thanks. Once Ravi lands quantization numbers we can finalize pricing guardrails. If quantization improves perf 2x, price/cost falls ~30% — we should model both conservative and optimistic scenarios.
Lena (Support): For concierge pilot: recommend 1 dedicated Slack channel + daily 9am sync for first week. Also need a template for customer onboarding emails. Priya, can you add that?
Priya (Docs): Yes. I'll add templates + a short troubleshooting triage flow. Will link the escalation command and sample logs to capture.
Jordan (PM): Ownership so far: SLA & runbook -> Sam; Surge policy & fallback -> Ravi; Concierge staffing -> Lena; Budget + pricing guardrails -> Marcus; Docs + public pages -> Priya; Security blurb -> Olivia. I'll update the staffing matrix. Please add any sub-owners inline.
Olivia (Security): I'll put a 2-day turnaround for the KMS paragraph. If compliance asks for more, we'll escalate to legal.
Ravi (Eng): Adding a note: we need a final perf sweep on Dedicated hardware (96hr burst test) before we lock SLA numbers. Can eng-qa help schedule?
Jordan (PM): Eng-QA: @rachel-qa can you help schedule the 96hr test next week? (cc @rachel-qa)
Sam (SRE): Also: define monitoring thresholds in the console — token-level cost alert at 20% over forecast, request-error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m, and KV cache miss spike > 30%. Those should trigger paged alerts to platform-oncall.
Marcus (FinOps): Add finance alerts: daily cost burn > forecast triggers a Slack post to #finops-alerts and an email to billing@redwood.com. Priya — include the notification copy in docs.
Lena (Support): Can we lock on who handles initial billing disputes during pilot? Support or FinOps? We need a clear path.
Marcus (FinOps): FinOps will triage charge dispute, Support does customer comms. We'll coordinate.
Jordan (PM): Outstanding blockers list I'm tracking: (1) quantization profile finalization (Ravi) (2) perf sweep scheduling (Rachel/Eng-QA) (3) budgets for concierge OT (Marcus) (4) public SLA wording decision (Priya + Legal) (5) KMS/residency blurb (Olivia). Please add ETA next to each.
Ravi (Eng): ETA quantization profile: 48h. Marking as high risk.
Priya (Docs): Let's keep public SLA wording high-level (percentile ranges) and publish details in an internal doc. Will coordinate with Legal.
Olivia (Security): SOC timeline: 6 weeks if requested. KMS blurb: 48h.
Marcus (FinOps): Budget decision: EOD tomorrow after I run the conservative/optimistic burn.
Jordan (PM): Thanks all. Action items: everyone drop a one-line ETA into the staffing matrix doc and I'll run a final sweep Friday. If anyone can't make their ETA, ping me directly. :thumbsup: 
Ravi (Eng): Added ETA.
Priya (Docs): Added templates + WIP public wording.
Lena (Support): Rota posted.
Sam (SRE): Runbook draft uploaded. Please review for missing playbook steps.
Jordan (PM): Closing the thread for now — I'll post a summary and final owners when I consolidate. If urgent, DM me. :lock:
